question.text: A call option writer receives a premium of Rs. 3 at a strike of Rs. 100. At expiry, the bond price is Rs. 106. What is the writer's net loss?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the workbook's short-call payoff table, the writer's exercise payoff = -(max(0, 106 - 100)) = -Rs. 6. Premium received offsets this loss: Net P&L = 3 - 6 = -Rs. 3 (loss of Rs. 3). The Trap: Rs. 6 ignores the premium received. Rs. 9 incorrectly adds the premium to the loss instead of offsetting it. Note: Consistent with the workbook's BEP discussion, the break-even point for the call writer is Strike + Premium = Rs. 103, so a settlement of Rs. 106 sits Rs. 3 beyond BEP -- exactly the net loss.
